newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse extends gains, awaits KGHM debut.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse extends gains, awaits KGHM debut.

text.p: The Polish bourse rose for the fourth session running on Tuesday and analysts said investors were awaiting the Thursday debut of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA to see if significant growth could follow.
The domestic-investor tranche of KGHM's recent public offering was 62-percent oversubscribed, the institutional tranche 22-percent oversubscribed.

"The market situation depends on the KGHM result -- if the debut is relatively high there'll be profit-taking and maybe a return of some of the money to the market," said Aleksander Jawien, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) brokerage.
But analysts said the relatively low institutional oversubscription augured a modest debut for the world's fifth largest electrolytic copper producer.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.3 percent to 15,735.7 points and turnover eased 3.4 percent to 145.1 million zlotys ($44 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 44 to 36 with 29 stocks flat.

Analysts said the overall market's stronger buying after price fixing signalled a gain on Wednesday but that signals outside the bourse, such as September's parliamentary elections and the generally good macroeconomic environment, were mixed.

Bank Handlowy rose 3.3 percent to 43.4 zlotys ($13.2) on Tuesday in continued heavy trade but analysts said the stock may be approaching its first fall since opening a week ago Monday 8.3 percent above issue.
Analysts said loss leader Izolacja, down 6.3 percent, fell in profit-taking after recent falls but that the construction materials maker still looked fundamentally sound.
